title: Internal-to-sectionwise normalization of the scalar projection mate
statement:
Let $a:\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a map of commutative condensed rings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], with exact scalar extension on every scheme, and let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Use small pro-etale sites in the coefficient universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. For $Z=X,Y$ put $R_Z=p_Z^*\Lambda$, $S_Z=p_Z^*\Lambda'$, with maps $a_Z$ and their canonical cartesian coefficient identifications and commuting coefficient-change squares [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]. Let $E_Z^R,E_Z^S$ be the canonical equivalences from internal module objects to section-ring module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Use the relative sheaf tensor, ordinary unbounded derived categories, K-flat tensor and K-injective direct image [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories, sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pur-kinjective-complex].

Termwise $E_Z^R,E_Z^S$ induce exact derived equivalences, preserve and reflect K-injectivity and K-flatness, and identify resolutions, total tensor complexes and their localized pure-tensor comparisons. They identify the specified internal geometric adjunctions with the canonical section-ring derived adjunctions, including units and counits. They also identify coefficient restriction and derived scalar extension, including the canonical pullback/tensor arrow used in their counit transposes.

Write $U_Z:D(S_Z)\to D(R_Z)$ for restriction, $T_Z=S_Z\otimes^L_{R_Z}-$, and $L_R\dashv G_R$, $L_S\dashv G_S$ for the geometric adjunctions in the section model. Let $d:U_YG_S\cong G_RU_X$ be the canonical composition comparison, and let $\gamma_C:T_YG_RC\to G_ST_XC$ be the internal coefficient-change map, transported by the above equivalences: its $S$-adjunct is the canonical pullback/tensor identification followed by $T_X(\varepsilon_{R,C})$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. For every $C\in D(R_X)$,
$$d_{T_XC}\circ U_Y(\gamma_C)=\delta_{S_Y,C},$$
where $\delta_{S_Y,C}:S_Y\otimes^L_{R_Y}G_RC\to G_R(S_X\otimes^L_{R_X}C)$ is the symmetric projection map whose $R$-adjunct is
$$L_R(S_Y\otimes^L G_RC)\cong S_X\otimes^L L_RG_RC\xrightarrow{1\otimes\varepsilon_{R,C}}S_X\otimes^L C.$$
This is equality of the specified morphisms under the canonical identifications. Restriction $U_Y$ is conservative. No properness, finite-type, boundedness or invertibility of $\gamma_C$ is assumed.

Its $e$ identifies $U_ZT_Z$ with $S_Z\otimes^L_{R_Z}-$ naturally on all derived morphisms, and its square identifies $U_X(\lambda_A)b_{T_YA}^{-1}$ with the canonical tensor pullback $\nu_A:L_R(S_Y\otimes^L A)\to S_X\otimes^L L_RA$ under those identifications.

proof.text: Put $A=G_RC$ and $t=T_X(\varepsilon_{R,C})\lambda_A$. By step 2 its $S$-adjunct is the specified transported $\gamma_C$. The transpose clause of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] identifies the $R$-adjunct of $U_X(t)b_{T_YA}^{-1}$ with $d_{T_XC}U_Y(\gamma_C)$. Step 4 computes the former map as $(1\otimes\varepsilon_{R,C})\nu_A$, the defining transpose of $\delta_{S_Y,C}$. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] gives the required equality. No invertibility of either projection or coefficient/direct-image map was used.
